interpretations.rationale: Present conclusion: a follower that accepts an InstallSnapshot whose index does not exceed its own cached last log index is left advertising a log it no longer holds; it then fails every prev-log check from that leader and accepts no further log entry, while the leader retries the same snapshot over and over. Source basis: installSnapshot sets lastApplied, lastSnapshot and the configurations but never lastLog (src_install_snapshot_tail, raft.go 1837-1977, tail at 1952-1977); getLastEntry prefers the cached log tail whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex (src_get_last_entry, state.go 160-174); the non-monotonic compaction path keeps the suffix above the snapshot index (src_compaction, snapshot.go 217-279); prev-log verification then misses below the store's first index or mismatches the stale suffix (src_append_prev_check, raft.go 1458-1606); the leader can only walk nextIndex down one step per rejection (src_replicate_failure, replication.go 240-300) until setupAppendEntries reports ErrLogNotFound, which jumps to SEND_SNAP and, on acceptance, resets nextIndex to snapshotIndex+1 (src_send_snapshot_result, replication.go 352-372). Retained observations, two independent runs of the same two-case experiment (executions 5e63769a85ac4b5f90ebe12a4ddcc5fd and d1897256143f4de2b0477a3460ae392b, both exit 0 with both cases passing): in the trimmed case the setup event (index 0) records the victim's cached claim at (95, term 2) with the leader's snapshot at 83/term 3, its store 1-95 intact and zero restores; after reconnect the probe event (index 14) records the victim's FSM restored 4 -> 1193 times inside the 3s window with the leader's snapshot index still 83 (repeated_snapshot_installs true, comparison 0 complete and holds), the victim's applied index unchanged at 83 while the cluster frontier reached 95 through newly committed and applied writes (victim_not_caught_up true, comparison 1 complete and holds on the same probe), the cached claim still (95, term 2) with the store suffix 84-95 kept, the victim's commit index still 0, and one stable leader set for the whole window with the victim's term fixed at 3. The untrimmed control on the same history (setup index 15, probe index 29) accepted no snapshot at all (restores 0, repeated_snapshot_installs false), repaired the claim with entries (95, term 3) and caught up (applied 83 -> 95, commit 95), which attributes the stall to the install path together with the trimmed leader log rather than to the mere existence of a stale suffix. The residual uncertainty is narrow and mechanical: comparisons 2, 3 and 4 are not yet decided because those definitions lack an applicability condition, so the other case's probe is treated as a missing admission; the third experiment adds the tag-scoped condition and is the discriminator for a complete verdict. Limits: three voters, InmemStore plus FileSnapshotStore, TrailingLogs=10 versus a large control, a 3s window with one write per 250ms sample, and a single induced partition; the follower's commit index was never advanced by the install path (0 while applied was 83) and is treated as an advertised-state inconsistency rather than an independent defect; the vote-side consequence of the stale claim is source-derived and unmeasured because no election occurred; the starved state would end if the leader later shipped a snapshot whose index exceeded the follower's cached claim, and no such snapshot was taken in either run because automatic snapshotting was disabled; the monotonic-store variant deletes the suffix instead of keeping it and needs its own receipt.

counterevidence: The untrimmed control accepted no snapshot (restores 0), repaired the stale suffix with ordinary log entries and reached the cluster frontier (applied 83 -> 95, commit 95): a stale suffix alone does not stall replication, so the snapshot-install path with a trimmed leader log is the trigger.

A successful InstallSnapshot refreshes the follower's last contact, so the follower never campaigned: both receipts show one stable leader set for the whole window and the victim's term fixed, so the starved state is stable rather than self-healing by election in this configuration.

The starved state is not proven unrepairable in principle: a later snapshot whose index exceeds the follower's cached claim would restore getLastEntry consistency. Neither run produced one because automatic snapshotting was disabled, and no such repair appears inside the measured window.
Comparisons 2, 3 and 4 remain unknown rather than holds in this receipt; the raw control fields recorded at index 29 carry the expected values, but no evaluated comparison yet establishes them.
limitations: Measured configuration only: three voters, InmemStore plus FileSnapshotStore, TrailingLogs=10 against a large control, an idle cluster with one write per 250ms sample, a 3s observation window and a single induced full partition of one voter.
The vote-side consequence of the stale claim is source-derived and unmeasured; no election was induced while the victim held the claim.
The monotonic-store path (delete-all-log store) deletes the stale suffix instead of keeping it, so its failure mode, other TrailingLogs values, larger clusters and longer windows are unmeasured here.

Probe fields are the follower's cached state, its log store range and its FSM restore counter, all read in-process; the follower's commit index staying 0 while its applied index was 83 is reported as an advertised-state inconsistency and not as an independent defect.

scope.description: Unchanged two-case experiment: two real three-voter cluster histories in one process where a leader is isolated and appends entries that never reach a quorum, is shut down, and the remaining voters elect a leader, commit further entries and take a snapshot; the isolated node is restarted on its unchanged in-memory log store and reconnected. The trimmed case (TrailingLogs=10) can only be repaired by the snapshot; the control (large TrailingLogs) can be repaired by entries. Each case samples restores, applied and commit index, cached last log entry, last snapshot and store range plus the cluster frontier for 3s of steady new writes.
assumptions: Fault model unchanged: no message loss inside the injected transport; the only induced event is a full transport partition of one voter plus its clean shutdown and restart on the same stores.

Reused facilities unchanged: MakeClusterCustom/MakeClusterOpts with inmemConfig timings, InmemStore, FileSnapshotStore, InmemTransport, MockFSM wrapped by a counting Restore, and the NewRaft restart pattern used by TestRaft_SnapshotRestore_Progress.
The victim's orphan suffix again comes from real Apply calls it accepted as leader while partitioned and survives the restart because the node replays its real log store.
Only the comparison definitions change in this revision; the harness file is byte-identical to the previous fixed artifact.
excluded: No production logic was modified; the harness only adds a test file.
Automatic snapshotting remains disabled (SnapshotThreshold huge, SnapshotInterval 1h) so the leader's snapshot index is controlled by the explicit Snapshot() call.

experiment.prefix: Identical to the previous revision, which ran both cases to completion with the same decisive values: build the cluster with MakeClusterCustom (counting FSM), commit 60 entries, partition the leader, fire 60 applies that never reach a quorum, wait for it to step down, shut it down, wait for one remaining voter to be the only stable leader, commit 20 further entries, force Snapshot(), record the snapshot and trimmed store range, restart the victim with NewRaft on its original stores and a fresh InmemTransport, reconnect it, emit ca_setup with tag plus the premise fields, wait for the first install, sample every 250ms for 3s while applying one entry per sample on the leader, emit ca_probe, then disconnect the victim before bounded teardown.
experiment.requirement: A follower that reinstalls the leader's snapshot must remain able to accept subsequent log entries from that leader, or its cached log state must not claim entries the snapshot superseded.

comparisons.description: Trimmed case: the follower's FSM was restored again after the first install, i.e. the same snapshot index was re-shipped during the window, while the leader's snapshot index is unchanged.
Trimmed case progress predicate: after the window the follower's applied index is still below the cluster frontier even though new entries committed and were applied elsewhere.
Trimmed case: the follower's cached last log index is still at or beyond the installed snapshot index with a lower term, and its store still holds that suffix.
Control: with an untrimmed leader log no snapshot is installed, separating the trigger from the existence of a stale suffix.
Control: the same cluster history without log trimming is repaired by log entries alone and the follower reaches the cluster frontier.

experiment.revision_reason: The second run decided the two trimmed-case comparisons as complete holds, but comparisons 2, 3 and 4 stayed unknown because a comparison with no applicability condition counts the other case's probe event as a failed admission ('No corresponding prerequisite events reached'), so missing_indices gained the other case's probe. Every comparison now carries a non-reference applicability condition on the mode field tag, which scopes each result event to its own case and records the other case's probe as outside applicability. Harness, scenario, anchors, assertions and test selection are unchanged.
semantic_changes: All five comparisons now carry a non-reference applicability condition on tag ('trimmed' or 'untrimmed'), scoping each result event to its own case so the other case's probe is outside applicability rather than a missing admission.
